root_cause.text: In `af_alg_alloc_tsgl()` the AF_ALG scatter/gather chaining code failed to clear the `end` marker on the last `struct scatterlist` entry of a full `af_alg_tsgl`, so `sg_chain()` linked a new list onto an SGL that still appeared terminated and `scatterwalk` later hit `sg_next()` returning NULL.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `sg_unmark_end(sg + MAX_SGL_ENTS - 1);` immediately before `sg_chain(sg, MAX_SGL_ENTS + 1, sgl->sg);`, and the CVE description says a sendmsg() that exactly fills `MAX_SGL_ENTS` leaves the last entry marked as end, causing a premature end and NULL dereference in scatterwalk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix scatterlist chaining by unmarking the previous end entry before linking in the new scatterlist segment.
intent_record.what: In af_alg_alloc_tsgl(), the conditional block that chains a newly allocated scatterlist into an existing one was expanded from a single sg_chain() call to a braced block that first calls sg_unmark_end(sg + MAX_SGL_ENTS - 1) and then calls sg_chain(sg, MAX_SGL_ENTS + 1, sgl->sg).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this clears the end marker on the last scatterlist entry before chaining, allowing the array to be treated as a proper chain instead of terminating early; this prevents scatterlist traversal from stopping at the wrong element and ensures the newly allocated tail scatterlist is reachable.

grouping_result.intent: Fix scatterlist chaining by unmarking the previous end entry before linking in the new scatterlist segment.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it clears the previous scatterlist end marker before chaining a new segment, which fixes the AF_ALG sg_chain/scatterwalk NULL-next failure.

candidates.rationale: This is the chaining operation that links a new scatterlist segment onto the previous one. If the prior last entry still had its end marker set, sg_chain() would attach to an SGL that appeared terminated, causing later sg_next() traversal to fail.

This initializes a full scatterlist segment, including the terminal entry state. The bug stems from not clearing the previous segment's end marker before chaining, so the segment initialization context is directly involved in the faulty SGL setup.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the chaining operation that attaches a new scatterlist segment to the previous one without first clearing the previous segment's end marker, which caused sg_next() traversal to encounter a NULL termination unexpectedly.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this function body. In the shown `af_alg_alloc_tsgl()` implementation, when a new TX SGL is appended, the code explicitly chains only after allocating a new list and does not leave a stale end marker visible in the snippet: `if (sg) sg_chain(sg, MAX_SGL_ENTS + 1, sgl->sg);`. More importantly, the later send paths in the same diff clearly add the missing end-marker handling that fixes the issue: `if (sgl->cur) sg_unmark_end(sg + sgl->cur - 1);` before adding more entries, and `sg_mark_end(sg + sgl->cur - 1);` when finishing a filled list in `af_alg_sendmsg()`; similarly `sg_mark_end(sgl->sg + sgl->cur);` in `af_alg_sendpage()`. Since the bug was specifically that the last `scatterlist` entry of a full `af_alg_tsgl` kept its end marker and `sg_chain()` linked onto an SGL that still appeared terminated, the shown code does not contain that buggy construct and already shows the corrective unmarking/marking logic in the consolidated send functions.
